geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the split-wing logic with a terrace operation to preserve the dominant gesture while making the upper mass read as occupiable and sectionally programmatic.
Orient the terrace movement along the long axis so the mass remains continuous and better aligned to the site figure.
Use a modest number of terrace levels to avoid an over-composed, stair-like silhouette.
Create a readable but restrained profile break that can support usable terrace space without turning into a generic code stepback.
Keep the secondary projection consistent with the main terrace direction to preserve one dominant spatial rule.
Soften the secondary terrace offset to reduce visual collision and improve continuity across views.

graph_edits.rationale: Retarget the dominant BOOK projection away from a split-wing reading and toward a calmer terrace-link continuity that can support a clearer ground/public threshold.
Enable a grounded spine so the mass responds to the access edge with a legible public seam rather than a sealed wedge.
Remove the overly bridge-like split cue; the candidate needs a cleaner anchor and less fragmentary upper separation.
Reduce wing separation so the form reads as one dominant mass with a controlled void instead of two competing pieces.
Tighten the secondary split further to improve form continuity and avoid a fractured stepped silhouette.
Lower the upper split mass to keep the section calmer and more plausible for neighborhood living.

rationale: The candidate reads as one primary elongated mass with a carved court, so it has some gesture clarity and void logic. However, the stepped/triangulated roof language is overly close to an arbitrary wedge/cascading object and does not convincingly resolve into a calm neighborhood-living section. Across the four views the form is coherent enough as a single object, but the section remains semantically weak: the roof and upper mass do not clearly support an active mixed-use ground threshold or a legible public terrace/court sequence. The blue frontage edge is acknowledged only weakly; the mass does not strongly open to it. Result: a plausible massing fragment, but not yet program-fit for the brief.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller and tower-like than the candidate; transfer the sectional taper logic, not the vertical scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A singular prismatic mass can keep a clear base and a tapered/stepped upper edge without losing overall coherence.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much smaller and more object-like; useful for frontage clarity, not for the candidate’s overall mass ratio.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact street-facing volume can read as neighborhood-serving when it keeps a clean ground threshold and a distinct vertical accent.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Larger and more complex; imitate the public void/terrace continuity, not the ring-building scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A continuous mass with a meaningful courtyarded void and stepped upper relationship can support neighborhood living without fragmenting the whole.

warnings: Visible massing is not strongly oriented to the verified access edge.
Section reads more like a sculpted wedge than a neighborhood-living building with active ground/public threshold logic.
Do not reward the stepped silhouette as a good section unless it clearly becomes occupiable and program-meaningful.
